additions.site_name: Green Mountain LON-East data centre campus (Romford North Data Centre), King George Close, Romford (Havering)
additions.name: Green Mountain LON-East (Romford) - 14 MW AI-ready data-hall expansion inside the existing building (delivered)

status.summary: Green Mountain's release dated 1 September 2026 announces a customer agreement for 14 MW at its LON-East campus in Romford, East London, under which a neocloud operator will occupy 'the recently delivered 14 MW of AI-ready capacity'. This dated operator disclosure supports completed status, as of 1 September 2026, for the 14 MW expansion: in Green Mountain's December 2023 description, six data halls built in two 7 MW phases inside the existing building. Completion keeps that scope. The customer's occupation is future, so operation of the new capacity is not asserted, and the campus's 37 MW planned total, its legacy 7 MW operation and the planned further building across King George Close are outside this project.

locator.precision: Site location published by the Environment Agency's installations register for permit EPR/FP3630EU (holder Green Mountain DC UK Limited, 'Romford North Data Centre, Unit 3 King George close, Romford, RM7 7PN'): grid reference TQ5027089800, latitude 51.587017, longitude 0.167675, copied without transformation. It lies inside Havering's 3.47 ha planning polygon for the existing data storage facility at 3 King George Close and locates the campus's existing building; it is not a building outline or surveyed position.
locator.identity_review: The register names the permit holder Green Mountain DC UK Limited at 'Romford North Data Centre', King George Close, Romford; the Environment Agency's 29 April 2026 inspection report for the same permit records Green Mountain DC UK Limited as operator and discusses the new data halls' generators; Green Mountain's 8 June and 1 September 2026 releases identify its Romford campus as LON-East and say Green Mountain DC UK owns the eight-acre site; and Green Mountain's December 2023 release says the site came with Infinity Data Centres in January 2023 (consistent with the 'ISDC Development' premises name in the register address) and that the 14 MW expansion was built inside the existing building. Havering's permission P1238.23 for a fin wall to 'the existing data storage facility' at 3 King George Close carries a 3.47 ha polygon that contains the register point (shapely 2.1.1: 62 m inside, 22 m from its centroid). In Esri World Imagery viewed locally (not redistributed) the point falls on a large pale-roofed industrial building with rooftop plant and a southern plant yard. A pyproj 3.7.1 transform of the register's easting and northing lands 0.77 m from the published point, and the RM7 7PN postcode centroid is 88 m away, so the point is not a postcode default. No geocoder, town centre or estate centroid is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The register publishes no positional accuracy; the point lies inside the 3.47 ha existing-facility planning polygon, and the 14 MW data halls occupy part of the existing building around it, not a separately located structure.

additions.distinctness_review: Screened on 27 October 2026 against all 830 sites and 894 projects, the evidence records, source records and identity mapping of verified_construction_core/2026-10-27-research-ninetyninth (site/config.json read ninety-eighth at the start of this pass and ninety-ninth when the screen was repeated before finishing), every sources/*-holds.json file, all other queue fragments' changes and holds, and claims.tsv, for Green Mountain, LON-East, Romford, King George Close, RM7 7PN, Infinity, ISDC, EPR/FP3630EU, Havering, P1238.23 and P1029.26. No Atlas record, hold or queued change names this campus: the Atlas Green Mountain records are its Norwegian and Mainz campuses, and the 'King George' matches are King George County, Virginia. No Atlas site, queued addition or other claim lies within 2 km; the nearest Atlas sites are the Charlton data centre proposal (14.2 km) and the Telehouse London Docklands campus (14.4 km). The only nearby data-centre records are Green Mountain's own planned building plot at 5 King George Close (about 160 m south-east), which is part of this campus and is not added here.
additions.successor_review: Re-checked on 27 October 2026: Green Mountain's post sitemap has no UK or LON-East post after the 1 September 2026 release (later posts concern Oslo, Norway and recruitment), and its LON-East page was last modified on 1 September 2026; the Environment Agency's compliance-document list for EPR/FP3630EU holds only the February 2026 data review and the 7 May 2026 inspection report; Havering's section 73 application P1029.26 for the separate planned building is undecided in the London Planning Datahub. No later record of commissioning, operation, suspension or change to the 14 MW expansion was found, so the 1 September 2026 completed observation is kept.

aliases: former Infinity Data Centres Romford site
scoped_project_details.facility_scope: 14 MW of new AI-ready data-hall capacity (two 7 MW phases, six data halls with over 5,500 sq m of white space) built inside the existing data-centre building (built 2009, about 11,000 m2) on Green Mountain's eight-acre LON-East campus at King George Close, Romford; the building's legacy 7 MW operation and the planned new building at 5 King George Close are outside this project
scoped_project_details.planning: Existing data storage facility at 3 King George Close (Havering P1238.23, external fin wall approved 6 October 2023); the separate planned data storage warehouse and emergency energy centre at 5 King George Close (P1137.11 of 2012, varied by P0614.20 of 14 January 2021) is subject to section 73 application P1029.26, validated 28 August 2026 and undecided
scoped_project_details.parties: Green Mountain DC UK Limited (Environment Agency permit holder and operator; freehold owner from 2026); the 14 MW customer is an unnamed neocloud operator
scoped_project_details.capacity_basis: 14 MW is Green Mountain's stated delivered capacity of the expansion (described in 2023 as 7 MW of IT load per phase); 37 MW is the campus's planned total and secured power, not built capacity

status.summary: The Environment Agency opened a consultation on 24 September 2026 (closed 22 October 2026) on Amazon Data Services UK Limited's bespoke permit application EPR/TP3621MM/A001 for the Ridgeway Data Centre Emergency Back Up Generation Facility, Ridgeway Trading Estate, Iver SL0 9JQ. This dated regulator record shows the Ridgeway data-centre development still live as a named, pending project on 24 September 2026, newer than the existing 13 August 2026 advertisement. The permit application is undecided and no Buckinghamshire planning decision or site work is asserted, so the status stays announced.

status_updates.identity_review: Same project as the existing record 'AWS Ridgeway Data Centre, Iver', whose 13 August 2026 announced status rests on the GOV.UK advertisement of the same application EPR/TP3621MM/A001 and whose locator comes from that application's non-technical summary (v3, 10 June 2026). The 24 September page names the same applicant, permit reference, facility ('Ridgeway Data Centre Emergency Back Up Generation Facility') and address (Ridgeway Trading Estate, Iver, SL0 9JQ) and lists the same application documents; the Environment Agency's consultation finder (local eac/finder-dc-b30.html and finder-data-centre.html) lists it separately from the consultation opened on 13 August 2026 that the Atlas already cites. No new building, phase, site, locator or capacity is implied.
status_updates.successor_review: Strictly newer than the existing 13 August 2026 observation. Re-checked on 27 October 2026: the consultation closed on 22 October 2026; the Environment Agency installations register has no registration EPR/TP3621MM (the full register read by uk-england-p4 on 27 October 2026 does not list it, a direct request for registration EPR-TP3621MM.json returned HTTP 404 on 27 October 2026, and no registration is dated 27 October), so no permit has been issued; Buckinghamshire Council's planning portal disallows all agents in robots.txt and its committee host serves a challenge (thirty-fourth holds), so a planning decision cannot be read and permitted status is not asserted. No AWS, Environment Agency or council record of works at Ridgeway was found. The 24 September 2026 announced observation is kept.
